#3421. Apple memory supplier expects price increases through at least 2030

Key Apple memory supplier SK Hynix has warned that RAM and flash memory shortages are likely to last through at least 2030, keeping product prices high.

Apple is believed to be one of 14 customers who have locked in priority orders, but the contract does not protect against price increases related to the balance of supply and demand …

The company says that while AI continues to drive demand and growth, there is little that can be done in the short to medium term to increase supply.

Supply, on the other hand, is not keeping pace with the growth of the market. Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.

The Register reports that SK Hynix has long-term deals with 14 tech giants for priority orders, but these allow for market-based price increases.

14 big buyers […] will collectively buy more than half of its output during 2027 and 2028, and some of them want to extend those agreements. The Korean giant doesn’t mind that because the deals include “a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers”

Apple is used to being in the driving seat when it comes to negotiating with suppliers, but this is not the case where memory and flash storage is concerned. Here, the shortages mean that it will have been forced to agree to contracts that allow significant price hikes in order to obtain guaranteed supplies.

Nikkei Asia also reports that printed circuit boards may be the next component to experience constrained supply. Once a humble commodity item, advances in the technology has turned them into specialist tech, with more layers and higher bandwidth requirements. The report says “that complexity shrinks the supplier pool and extends lead times.”

Apple said back in June that the company was doing its best to mitigate the price increases, but it has so far been unable to do so.

#3420. NFL’s Jack Campbell Hospitalized After Being Unable to Move on Field

NFL player Jack Campbell remains in the hospital after he suffered a neck injury in the Lions’ game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1.

The Detroit Lions are navigating a harrowing injury.

While the NFL team secured a victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1, they suffered a terrifying moment in the fourth quarter when linebacker Jack Campbell went down after his third tackle of the game.

Campbell was lying face down in the field and seemingly unable to move after tackling Vikings player T.J. Hockenson. Medical personnel rushed to evaluate his injuries and eventually strapped the 26-year-old to a backboard, transporting him off the field as fans applauded.

Many of Campbell’s teammates and coaching staff surrounded the cart that carried him as he was taken for further evaluation. His wife Megan Campbell and their newborn baby boy were reportedly brought down to the field level to travel with him in the ambulance.

Following the game, the Lions shared an update on the NFL star, writing on X, “Jack Campbell is being transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.”

An additional update shared by the team confirmed Campbell would remain in the hospital overnight for further evaluation and promised to share additional updates when available.

Meanwhile, the Lions’ head coach Dan Campbell (no relation) also addressed his player’s injury in a press conference following the game.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family,” he said, per NBC Sports. “He’s being taken care of. We don’t have any new information. We’ll keep you updated as this goes, but we’re thinking about him.”

The terrifying scenario comes after news of a similarly dangerous injury rocked the NFL world.

On Oct. 19, it was confirmed that the Philadelphia Eagles’ quarterback Jalen Hurts would likely be out for the entire season after being diagnosed with bilateral blood clots in his lungs as well as deep vein thrombosis from a calf injury.

At the time, his agent Nicole Lynn confirmed Hurts was “clinically stable,” but that he would not be able to participate in football at this time.

“His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. ‘blood thinners’),” she shared in her statement. “We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners.”

“In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition,” Lynn added. “More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.”

For more stars who have experienced terrifying accidents, read on.

Jamie Lynn Spears' then-8-year-old daughter Maddie Aldridge was driving an ATV in February 2017 when she accidentally flipped it into a pond near their Louisiana home, leaving her submerged under water for minutes.

"When we were finally able to get her out of the water and I saw her and then the first responders took her from me, we thought she was gone," Jamie Lynn recalled on a 2020 episode of Maria Menounos Better Together podcast. "We thought we'd lost our daughter."

Though the family wasn't sure what sort of damage had been done, Maddie was awake and talking two days later. A few weeks after that, she was back to her normal routine.

"God gave me the blessing of giving me my daughter back," Jamie Lynn continued. "I lost her and I got her back."

Filming on Rebel Wilson and Anna Camp's 2025 action comedy Bride Hard turned dramatic during the Aussie's final day of playing secret agent. "In a fight scene, a gun accidentally got whacked across my face," Rebel explained to Access Hollywood in a June 2025 interview. "It was just a freak accident, and my nose got split open, so I left set. It was my last night of shooting. I was like, 'How unlucky can I be?'"

Surrounded by a pool of her own blood, "I was freaking out," she admitted of the 2023 incident. "They take an ambulance and they have to call a plastic surgeon, because if they didn’t, I would have been permanently disfigured. So we got the plastic surgeon, they did all the stitches, and you can’t tell now."

Tonight Show host Jimmy Fallon almost lost his finger after he tripped and fell in his own home. He tried catching himself on the counter and his ring got stuck on the way down, pulling his finger out.

He described it as "ring avulsion," and it kept him in the hospital for 10 days as doctors worked to prevent him from having to get it amputated.

An experienced hiker who competes in distance running, swimming and triathlons, Zane Wach was nearly felled by altitude sickness while hiking with his dad Ryan Wach on California's Mount Whitney in June 2025.

"He started to experience some hallucinations," Ryan explained to to the SFGATE of the 14-year-old. "He knew he was hallucinating. He said he saw things like snowmen and Kermit the Frog."

Ryan managed to stop his teen from walking off the cliff multiple times as they made their way back down the trail. “He was in an altered mental state, and I don’t know what caused it. We still don’t know,” the father noted. “My best guess is a combination of exhaustion, sleep deprivation, probably some dehydration and lasting effects from the altitude sickness. But he essentially started to doubt reality.”

And on a third attempt, Ryan was too far away to catch Zane, watching as his son fell roughly 120 feet off the cliff. After waiting six hours for an Inyo County Search & Rescue helicopter to get there and fly Zane to Southern Inyo Hospital in Lone Pine, he was stabilized and transferred to a pediatric trauma center in Las Vegas. Placed into a medically induced coma, he eventually began breathing on his own.

“It’s going to be a survival story in the end," Ryan said of his teen, who suffered head trauma along with a broken finger, ankle and fractured pelvis, "but right now we’re still in the middle of it."

On New Years' Day 2023, Avengers star Jeremy Renner was using a snowplow to tow a truck that was stuck in the snow on the driveway of his Lake Tahoe home. But after exiting the machine, he was pulled under while trying to stop the plow from hitting his nephew and suffered 38 broken bones.

"As I lay on the ice, my heart rate slowed, and right there, on that New Year’s Day, unknown to my daughter, my sisters, my friends, my father, my mother, I just got tired," he wrote in his 2025 memoir My Next Breath. "After about thirty minutes on the ice of breathing manually for so long, an effort akin to doing ten or twenty push-­ups per minute for half an hour . . . that’s when I died."

Fighting broken bones, blood loss and the threat of hypothermia, "I know I died—in fact, I’m sure of it," he wrote. “When the EMTs arrived, they noted that my heart rate had bottomed out at 18, and at 18 beats per minute, you’re basically dead."

TikToker Emilie Kiser and her husband Brady Kiser were forced to face the unimaginable when their 3-year-old son Trigg Kiser fell into the pool at their Arizona home in May 2025.

Chandler Police Department told USA Today that officers responded to a drowning call at a residence on May 12, for a child who had been pulled unconscious out of a backyard pool. Both police and firefighters administered CPR on the scene, before taking Trigg to Chandler Regional Hospital. But, sadly, the toddler died six days later.

Emilie later filed a lawsuit against Maricopa County public offices requesting that the court prohibit the public release of details surrounding his death. "Emilie is trying her best to be there for her surviving son, two-month-old Theodore," the lawsuit stated. "But every day is a battle."

A family vacation to Thailand turned into "the worst 10 days" of Dr. Cara Hodgson's life after she was electrocuted by power lines in December 2023. After blacking out and being rushed to the ER, the influencer spent the next week and a half "going in and out of hospitals fighting to regain my strength and fighting for my life," she detailed in a New Year's Day Instagram post. "I am so lucky to be here today."

As such, the orthodonist found a new reason to smile through the pain. The experience "taught me something I think we all need to be reminded of when we get caught up in the little things: What a precious privilege it is to be alive," Cara shared, "being able to breathe, eat, talk, move your body, is something grand and something to be celebrated."

Tragedy occured when Brazilian tourist Juliana Marins was hiking on Mount Rinjani, an active volcano in Indonesia, in June 2025. After she fell off a cliff (but not into the volcano's crater), a team of 48 search and rescuers spent four days "hindered by adverse weather, terrain and visibility conditions in the region," the Brazilian government shared in a statement, and eventually located Juliana's body.

"Today, the rescue team managed to reach the place where Juliana Marins was,” detailed a post on an Instagram account providing updates from her family. “With great sadness, we inform you that she did not survive. We remain very grateful for all the prayers, messages of affection and support that we have received."

When former Beverly Hills, 90210 star Tori Spelling attended a 2015 Easter brunch at Japanese restaurant Benihana, she tripped and burned her right arm on one of the Hibachi grills. After undergoing skin grafts to treat the injury, the actress ultimately deciding to sue the restaurant.

“I have a skin graft that they had to take from my leg," she later detailed on a 2024 episode of her and Jennie Garth's podcast 9021OMG. "Not many people can say, 'Hey, I'm wearing my thigh on my arm,' and I'm not even kidding. So I'm wearing a thin layer of my thigh on my arm because the skin burnt so bad."

When comedian Tony Knight attended France's Rock&Cars festival in June 2024, he was killed after two large branches fell from a tree. "He was only 54 and having the time of his life," Joanne Allen, the sister of Tony's longtime partner Hayley Wright detailed in a GoFundMe message. "He was fit, healthy, happy and had everything going for him. He was charismatic, funny, passionate."

And, of course, adored by his longtime love. "He was an exceptionally talented man, with so many strings to his bow," Haley wrote in her own Instagram post. "There really was nothing he couldn’t do. He was a fantastic friend to so many, an amazing dog Dad….but most of all he was my world & it will never be the same without him."

A company celebration turned catastrophic in January 2024. To kickoff the planned 25th anniversary festivities for Chicago-based software company Vistex, CEO Sanjay Shah and president Vishwanath Raju Datla were suspended in an iron cage meant to be lowered 20 feet onto a dais at the India-based party, a company official told The Times of India. Instead, two wires snapped, causing the men to crash onto the concrete stage.

Sanjay, 56, died of his injuries at the hospital following the accident, the paper reported, while 52-year-old Vishwanath sustained a severe head injury and passed months later.

"When I was 19 I fell three floors from a window and broke my back," Orlando Bloom shared in a joint 2022 Instagram video with UNICEF. He had been trying to climb to the rooftop terrace of a three-story building with friends when the drainpipe he was scaling collapsed. Though he broke several vertebrae in his back, "I was very fortunate to survive the fall because my spinal cord was still just intact."

Still, he detailed, "When I was in the hospital, I was told for the first four days that I may never walk again. That was really the beginning of what was a long and painful journey for me into recognizing and understanding some of the patterns that had been in my life that had led me to having numerous accidents. And the culmination was breaking my back, which was a near-death experience."

Leaving the hospital in a back brace with heaps of physical and emotional pain, "I started partying straight away—with the back brace on," he shared with GQ in 2005. "It took me a couple of months to realize this was my life, and I didn't want to mess it up."

The experience has "informed everything in my life," he added. "Until you're close to losing it, you don't realize. I used to ride motorbikes and drive cars like everything was a racetrack; it was ridiculous. It wasn't because I thought it was cool; it was just because I loved living on the edge. But I've chilled."

The crew member then responded that the aircraft was banking at 60 degrees ... before their audio cut out.

#3418. 10 Shows Like 'VisionQuest' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Following the events of WandaVision (and, slightly more tangentially, Agatha All Along), VisionQuest returns to the story of Marvel's favorite synthic being, an artificial creation who fights supervillains and ponders the nature of his own existence, rather than more typical AI pursuits like creating deep fakes.

White Vision (the character, not the political agenda) is a copy of the Vision who died two Avengers movies ago. He's living within his own mind on a fantasy country estate while on the run from bounty hunters and in pursuit of his semi-fictional son. In that spirit, here are 10 more science fiction shows that involve artificial people and/or elaborate constructed realities.

In the near-future world, highly advanced “synths” are commonplace, doing the work that regular humans can’t be bothered with. These beings are treated as entirely disposable sources of cheap labor, despite their apparent burgeoning humanity. The first season introduces the Hawkins family, who buy (on sale) a domestic servant synth named Anita (Gemma Chan); mom Laura is a little uncomfortable with the arrangement, especially when she finds her husband having sex with Anita, who has her own complicated backstory. Humans interrogates the ways humans always seem to find excuses to dehumanize others, which is just the type of thing that sci-fi is pretty great at. Stream Humans on Peacock, Prime Video, and Tubi.

One of the smartest recent shows is a dark comedy based on the Hugo-Award winning book series by Martha Wells. Alexander Skarsgård is the title's hilariously deadpan robot, a private "security construct" who's managed to hack its way through its own programming and gain free will—which it mostly wants to use to binge its favorite streaming shows. It can't just run off for fear of drawing attention, but the self-named Murderbot (it's being ironic, kinda) is content to do the bare minimum when it's assigned to a team of naive hippie researchers who don't see the need for a killer security robot—at least, not until they're enmeshed in a complicated capitalist plot in which they're all just cogs. Stream Murderbot on Apple TV.

From playwright Tearrance Arvelle Chisholm (Hooded: Or Being Black for Dummies), this show stars Okieriete Onaodowan as the title character, an inhabitant of an alternate present who is turning 33 and pursuing therapy for the first time. He's offered the chance to use DIRT (Digital Immersive Reality Therapy), in which he can visit and view other versions of himself, as long as he doesn't interfere. Which, of course, he does, with results that are sometimes poignant and sometimes funny. Hard to believe that this clever show almost wound up in the bin, a victim of that stupid moment a couple of years ago when streamers and studios were shelving otherwise great projects for tax reasons. No robots here, but a human exploring a complex world inside his own head. Stream Demascus on Tubi.

In this more darkly dangerous vision of a virtual world, video-game-obsessed Arisu gets his wish, after a fashion; he finds himself, along with a couple of friends, transported to an alternate, eerily abandoned version of Tokyo—the title’s Borderland—vividly brought to life via clever green screen work. The three are directed to an arena and given the instructions for the game, which they’ll be playing whether they want to or not. The first competition involves a locked-room-style puzzle; if they fail, the room goes up in flames with them in it—think Ready Player One, with deadlier stakes. There are games each night, though the rules allow for winners to get time off. There are a lot of rules, actually, but the games are cleverly and sadistically constructed. Stream Alice in Borderland on Netflix.

Though ostensibly an X-Men spinoff, this phantasmagoric show from Noah Hawley (Fargo, Alien: Earth) stands entirely on its own, taking place largely inside the headspace of a deeply troubled man. Dan Stevens plays David Haller, diagnosed with schizophrenia and possessed of tremendous psychic abilities. In one of the many psychiatric hospitals to which he's been committed, he meets first the free-wheeling Lenny (Aubrey Plaza) and then Syd (Rachel Keller), who can trade bodies with anyone she touches. Veering in and out of trippy astral planes and deeply damaged psyches, David soon comes to realize that he's not crazy—and also that he's probably not the hero of the story, even as he's caught between the authorities who'd like to use him for his power and the Shadow King who's been haunting his mind since childhood. Stream Legion on Hulu.

Just a science fiction action comedy about a nun married to literal Jesus on a quest to save the world from the title's artificial intelligence by finding the Holy Grail alongside her ex-boyfriend. So, yeah, there’s a lot going on in Mrs. Davis—sometimes a little too much, but the show gets major points for ambition. Betty Gilpin holds everything together as Sister Simone, playing it straight in an extremely over-the-top world. It’s refreshing to see a show that’s so unafraid to take big swings, and it works much more often than it should. Though it was cancelled after one season, it ends reasonably well, and, like co-creator Damon Lindelof’s HBO series Watchmen, would probably be best served by remaining a one-and-done. Stream Mrs. Davis on Peacock.

A charming comedy-drama set in a science fiction world, Robbie Amell stars as Nathan Brown, a young computer programmer who's also recently deceased. In the future of 2033, humans have the option of having their consciousnesses uploaded into virtual worlds post-mortem and Nathan's is chosen for him by his rich and rather possessive girlfriend. The exclusive afterlife setting of Lakeview is stifling, as is the fact that said girlfriend has a say in his perpetual existence. He's on the brink of despair until he strikes up a friendship with Nora (Andy Allo), his very-much-alive customer service rep. Stream Upload on Prime Video and Hulu.

Tricky to recommend, given that the show's four seasons saw a period of decline followed by a cancellation just when it was getting really good again—however, when Westworld was cooking (as in its addictive first season), there was nothing else like it on television. Set, initially, in a high-tech, near-future amusement park designed to appeal to wealthy clientele, the show finds the lifelike androids created to service the guests gradually waking up to their disposability. In the best tradition of sci-fi, this one's less about AI than it is about a world of disposable beings existing purely at the whim, and for the amusement of, the ultra-wealthy. Which is definitely not a 100% relatable metaphor. Buy Westworld from Prime Video.

You've likely seen this one if you're watching VisionQuest, but it's worth mentioning as not only a fairly essential preface, but also one of the best (and most distinctive) bits of Marvel media...ever? (Agatha All Along is also great, but less essential to Vision's narrative). At least initially, WandaVision confused dedicated Marvel fans as much as noobs, making it a unique on-ramp, even if it does have many threads connected to the broader superhero universe. Its story of a grieving witch living out her sitcom fantasies is an impressive swing into the surreal, well worth it if you’re content to go along for a weird and surprisingly emotional ride. Stream WandaVision on Disney+.

#3414. Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean Dead at 34 After Cancer Battle

Ciara Mageean, who competed for Ireland in track and field at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics, died after a battle with bowel cancer, her family announced Nov. 1.

The track and field community is mourning one of their own.

Two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean died Nov. 1 following a battle with bowel cancer, her family confirmed in a statement. She was 34.

"At 6:30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones," the statement shared on Instagram said. "A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed."

The post ended with a traditional Irish blessing, "ar dheis Dé go raibh a hanam," which translates to "may her soul be at the right hand of God."

Tributes poured in for Mageean—who represented Ireland in track and field at the 2016 Rio Olympics and the 2020 Tokyo Olympics—after her passing.

"We are devastated to hear about this loss to the world of sport," the Olympics' account commented under the post. "Our thoughts are with her family and friends at this sad time."

World Athletics, the international governing body for track and field, wrote, "Heartbreaking news. A fighter on and off the track. Our thoughts are with her family, friends and the entire athletics community. She will be deeply missed."

Mageean—who became the second person ever to win an individual European title for Ireland when she won the women's 1,500 meters race at the 2024 European Athletics Championships—first announced that she'd been diagnosed with cancer last year.

"Thank you for the love and strength," Mageean added at the time. "I’m ready to face this with the same fight I’ve always brought to the track."

She further detailed her diagnosis earlier this year when she shared that she specifically had stage 4 bowel cancer, which she first got tested for after noticing an uptick in the frequency of her bowel movements.

"I'll never forget that day on the 20th of May," she told RTE in an interview in June. "Going in to have what I thought was a routine little scope and I wouldn't find out results for a bit after. But instead on that very day, I found out that I had cancer."

"Because I'm so young and healthy, I thought I'll be at an early stage," Mageean added. "Not that any stage of cancer is okay."

The runner—who wed her partner Tommy Moran in an intimate civil ceremony in Northern Ireland weeks before her passing Oct. 12—was also reflective on what her diagnosis was potentially going to take away from her.

"I'm hopeful that I get to live into old age but the odds are stacked against me and that's really, really hard," Mageean said. "I am so grateful for the support of the Irish nation. It's been there for me throughout my entire career. But I feel supported and loved throughout this journey."

#3412. If You Loved 'Carrie,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Stephen King’s Carrie is one of those endlessly rebootable stories. Way back in 1974, King zeroed in on a near-perfect horror setup that explored being othered, the emotional and mental health consequences of bullying, and just how crappy being a teen girl can be in the modern world. Those themes—and the iconic visuals King conjured with his words—are evergreen, and resonate with audiences each time the story gets rebooted. Mike Flanagan has proved himself a master of horror and a clear successor to King’s legacy in the genre, and if you thought his Carrie reboot on Prime Video was terrific (and you’ve watched all the similar series out there), you should really watch Jennifer’s Body.

Carrie and Jennifer’s Body share a lot of themes—the corrosive pressure of high school, the casual cruelty of adolescents, the explosive power of feminine anger. While Jennifer Check (Megan Fox) is superficially presented as having more power and control than Carrie White (Summer H. Howell) because she’s more self-possessed (and played by Megan Fox), underneath the hair and makeup, Jennifer is just as naive and confused as Carrie. Both girls endure horrific experiences that set them on a path to horrific violence—and those experiences are symbolic of what women everywhere have to deal with all the damn time.

Just as in Carrie, Jennifer’s Body tracks a teen girl’s descent into monstrousness—but where Carrie leans into the tragic nature of those themes, Jennifer’s Body offers a funnier, more sarcastic take buoyed by Diablo Cody’s sharp dialogue and laugh-out-loud moments. The series highlights Carrie’s suffocating home life that offers her no relief from the grinding hell of being a 16-year-old girl who doesn’t quite fit the expected physical or behavioral norms imposed on teen girls, tracing a slow boil of rage. Jennifer’s Body depicts a character who ultimately chooses the dark path, leaning into her newfound destructive power, and has more fun with it, making it the perfect complement to the series.

Although the stories take different paths to get there, they both wind up at a cathartic and bloody climax centered on a school dance, where a lot of people die and chaos reigns. The film is the perfect way to examine, from a different angle, the themes that Carrie explores. Stream Jennifer’s Body on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

Looking for more stories about angry teen girls teaching society a terrifying lesson? Here are a few more films that make a perfect pairing with Carrie.

It’s been 50 years since Brian De Palma adapted King’s novel for the first time, and it’s still worth watching today, especially if you enjoyed Flanagan’s modern take. What could have been a trashy horror movie designed to cash in on the book’s success is instead a well-crafted film that makes every character feel real and consequential, and Sissy Spacek’s performance as Carrie is screen-meltingly amazing. Few horror films have aged this well, and watching a different creator’s vision of the story will be well worth your time. Rent Carrie on Prime Video.

If Carrie’s cathartic presentation of female rage and teen angst is what hooked you, the most relevant movie to jump to is The Craft. The story of four high school girls who harness dark powers to take revenge on, well, high school life itself is anchored by four feral performances from Robin Tunney, Fairuza Balk, Neve Campbell, and Rachel True. Like Jennifer’s Body, the teen protagonists enthusiastically embrace their power in a way that Carrie White doesn’t, but it transforms (and destroys them) just the same. Rent The Craft on Prime Video.

One reason Carrie is terrifying in all its forms? The very idea of a child with an imperfect grasp of ethics and an immature emotional state having thermonuclear-level psychic powers. After all, teenage girls without powers can be terrifying when triggered. The Innocents focuses on sisters Ida (Rakel Lenora Petersen Fløttum) and Anna (Alva Brynsmo Ramstad), who meet Ben (Sam Ashraf) and Aisha (Mina Yasmin Bremseth Asheim), who both demonstrate powers including telekinesis and mind control. Their interaction soon reveals that Anna also has mental powers, and the four begin working to enhance their capabilities—but when one of them begins using their powers to hurt others and seek revenge, things take a dark turn that fans of Carrie will appreciate. Stream The Innocents on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

Anyone who was ever bullied in the teen years (so ... everyone) knows that those wounds never quite heal. That’s one aspect of Carrie’s power, and it’s also what makes Sissy an ideal movie to watch when you’ve finished the series. A mental health influencer, Cecilia (Aisha Dee)—once known as “Sissy”—runs into her old best friend, Emma (Hannah Barlow) and is unexpectedly invited to Emma’s bachelorette weekend—only to run into her childhood tormentor, Alex (Emily De Margheriti). The old trauma hits Cecilia like a bomb, shattering her fragile mental balance and leading to a surprisingly funny series of murders as Sissy works through her lingering anger issues. Stream Sissy on Hoopla or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

If you’re a Mike Flanagan and Stephen King superfan, the obvious movie choice is their other collab, Doctor Sleep. A sequel to one of the most famous horror stories of all time (The Shining), the story finds a middle-aged Danny Torrance (Ewan McGregor) struggling to control his psychic powers, and leading the fight against an ancient group of entities that feed off of people like him. If you want more of that Flanagan/King magic, this is the right move. Rent Doctor Sleep on Prime Video.

Apple recently launched new HomePod mini speakers and its HomeView smart display, and today it’s Amazon’s turn with five new Alexa devices.

This includes a new Echo speaker with visual intelligence and an Echo Show with a larger 16-inch display and a nanomatte option …

The latest smart device lineup kicks off with a next-generation Echo Dot speaker, which includes a home hub, on-device AI capabilities, and a built-in Wi-Fi extender.

For the first time, it includes a built-in smart home hub, so Alexa connects to thousands of compatible devices such as lights, locks, and thermostats right out of the box—plus a built-in eero Wi-Fi extender adds up to 1,000 square feet of coverage to your existing network. At its core is Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon, with a new AI Accelerator for on-device AI that sharpens conversational detection and filters out background noise. Music, audiobooks, and podcasts sound great on the new Echo Dot, with crisp vocals and 50% more bass than its predecessor.

The Dot is available today for $99.99, with special Kids editions for $109.99 that include a one-year subscription to Amazon Kids+.

The Echo Studio is a better speaker that now includes HomePod-like room mapping and a camera that allows a live view of your home as well as Alexa-powered visual intelligence features.

Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon’s best-sounding speaker and gives it a richer understanding of the room around it, making Alexa even more useful. The same powerful audio architecture is still at its core—a high-excursion woofer and Dolby Atmos filling the room with immersive spatial sound, now continuously tuned to your space with Advanced Room Adaptation. Its new sleep sensing technology, powered by Omnisense, can sense when you’re in lighter sleep and wakes you within 10 to 60 minutes of your scheduled alarm, no wearable device required. Most of the photos we love never leave our phones. The Alexa Photo Frame changes that—pairing the timeless elegance of a traditional frame with the intelligence of Alexa, so your best memories are always on display. It’s the first photo frame with Alexa built in, and it works effortlessly: connect it to Amazon Photos and your pictures sync automatically, with new ones appearing as they’re taken. Alexa intelligently surfaces the shots worth seeing—the ones where you’re smiling, in the right season—and skips the screenshots and clutter. Just ask to see photos of a favorite person, pet, or trip, or swipe through right on the 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen, where every picture looks crisp and vibrant from any angle.

The all-new Echo Show 16 is our most advanced display yet, with 20% more power for interactions that feel fast. Screen Styles transform it into whatever your home needs most—a family organizer with color-coded calendars, chores, and meal plans; a digital photo frame; or a smart home dashboard with the new Alexa Home Map, showing every light, lock, thermostat, and camera right where it lives in your home. Plus, it has the full Fire TV experience, built in. Echo Show 16 has our best-ever camera on an Echo Show, featuring the widest field of view, auto-framing that keeps everyone in view, and—for the first time—night vision, so you can check in with Live View day or night.

The Echo Show 16 is available for pre-order today at $499.99 or $569.99 with the nanomatte screen. Availability hasn’t yet been confirmed, with the company simply saying that it will begin shipping “later this year.”

#3409. Google's 'Health Guardian' Is Now Available for Fitbits

Google’s “Health Guardian” feature set rolled out in late September to Pixel Watches 3, 4, and 5, and is now coming to Fitbit Air users in a new update. Google says the new features include reports on your blood pressure trends and on insulin resistance, which is a big claim for a wearable. Here’s what we know about Health Guardian, including how to set it up and what to expect.

Insulin resistance is associated with type 2 diabetes, and can be an early sign that you are heading toward pre-diabetes or diabetes. When your body’s insulin receptors stop responding as strongly to insulin, you’re more likely to have higher blood glucose.

Insulin resistance is normally measured with bloodwork. For example, your fasting glucose levels and fasting insulin are combined into a score called HOMA-IR. If you’re concerned about insulin resistance or pre-diabetes, it’s best to talk to an actual healthcare professional to find out what tests they recommend, and what to do with the results.

The insulin resistance feature coming to Google Health is, Google notes, “not intended for medical purposes” and “not a pre-screener for diabetes.”

Google published a paper describing some of the testing that went into developing its insulin resistance algorithm. In the study, the researchers had people use their own Fitbits or Pixel Watches to record a variety of metrics, including heart rate, HRV, and activity. It’s not clear from this paper exactly how the algorithm works or whether it’s likely to be useful in a general population, but apparently Google is betting on it being an interesting factor to track in your Google Health app.

Google also published a paper on a blood pressure algorithm, although it is not peer-reviewed. Instead of explaining how the algorithm works, it describes how the researchers tried to figure out what their AI-based model might be looking at. According to this paper, Google's model works about as well as clinical blood pressure measurements, but it's not clear how useful it would be in the real world. For example, the study excluded people with heart disease, but I'd imagine plenty of people with heart disease would be interested in their blood pressure scores.

Google said last month in a press release that Health Guardian, which includes insulin resistance and blood pressure trends, is available for free for people who use a Pixel Watch 3, 4, or 5. Fitbit Air users, they added, would get blood pressure and insulin resistance trends “with a Google Health Premium subscription later this year.” "Later" has arrived, as the feature for Fitbit users is in Google Health 5.11, available on both Android and iOS.

So it’s free if you have a Pixel Watch, but not if you only have the Fitbit Air: Google Health Premium is $9.99/month. It’s unclear what happens if you own both devices; presumably, having a Pixel Watch will get you free access. In any case, other devices, including older Fitbits, do not seem to be included.

The Pixel Watch got Health Guardian in the 5.09 release of the Google Health app for Android. The Fitbit got Health Guardian in the 5.11 release for both Android and iOS.

You can set up your blood pressure and insulin resistance tracking as soon as you get the new version of the Google Health app. I was able to set up insulin tracking by going to the health tab and then tapping Metabolic, and I set up blood pressure under Heart. If you go to Respiratory, you can also set up sleep-breathing quality. (Some European users will get a feature that can call for help in a "breathing emergency," but that is not available in the U.S.)

Google said that the insulin and blood pressure features will give you a monthly report on the first of each month, with the first report coming Oct. 1, if you have given the watch enough data in the previous month. If you're a Fitbit user and are just setting up the feature now, you'll get your first report on Nov. 1. Here is what the app requires:

For blood pressure reports: You need to wear the watch for five consecutive days in the previous month (so, in October to get your November report). You don't have to wear the watch at night.

For insulin resistance: You need to wear the watch for seven days and nights in the previous month, but they don't need to be consecutive.

I set up both features as soon as I got the update for the Pixel Watch, but that timeline didn't allow me a full seven days and nights before the October report. That means I don't have an insulin resistance result. I do have my blood pressure trend result: "Not High." As a reminder, a watch cannot know your actual blood pressure, so the watch is making estimates based on data that may not correspond with your actual blood pressure. That said, my blood pressure tends to read in the normal range at doctors' visits, so at least this wasn't surprising.

What's more confusing is what you're actually supposed to do about the results. If your watch says your blood pressure or insulin are fine, would you delay seeking care or abandon a treatment or lifestyle change that was supposed to help you? If your watch says something is wrong, would you believe that and maybe spend unnecessary time and money getting checked out? Pixel Watch users are discussing their results online, with a variety of reactions. One redditor says: "I awoke to find out that my blood pressure is too high and apparently the insulin in my body does nothing. This despite that my most recent doctor's visit and blood work were all perfectly normal." Another said: "I got this high insulin result this morning. I have really changed my diet the last four months and I have been going to the gym regularly. I have lost about 40 pounds this year. It's a bummer to see this. I just wonder if it's accurate." I wonder that, too.

What it’s like to use the iPhone Duo as my daily driver

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It’s one thing to test out a phone for a review, but it’s another to ditch your everyday phone for a foldable — especially one that still feels unfinished in some ways. Don’t get me wrong, the iPhone Duo at times feels magical, especially when I used it to binge watch Netflix on its massive screen during a flight and when regularly multitasking with two apps side by side (finally).

But during my two-week experiment of swapping out my iPhone 17 Pro Max for the iPhone Duo I did question whether I would upgrade to this device and spend $2,000 for it. Here’s what I really like about Apple’s first foldable so far, what needs work, and what it’s really like to live with it as your daily driver.

Apple has done an awesome job making the iPhone Duo as versatile as possible with its design. Unlike the Galaxy Z Fold 8, the hinge holds various angles well and the software morphs as you bend the device.

While on a recent business trip, I used the tent position to turn the Duo into my alarm clock in Standby mode. I also like to use the tabletop mode for FaceTime calls, as I usually like to pace around the room while I talk. My family likes to say I have “ants in my pants” so this helps!

iPhone Duo: up to $1,200 off w/ trade-in + unlimited @ T-MobileT-Mobile is knocking up to $1,200 off the iPhone Duo when you switch and bring your number or when you trade-in an eligible phone and sign up for a qualifying plan. The iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR display (1,878 x 2,670) and a 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR outer display (1,398 x 2,034). It houses Apple's A20 Pro chipset, 12GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and two 24MP front cameras. Rear cameras include a 48MP main (f/1.6) and 48MP ultrawide (f/2.2). In our iPhone Duo review, we called it the best designed foldable yet thanks to Apple's combination of polished design, robust software experience, and enhanced durability. Price check: $1,200 off @ Verizon | $1,200 off @ AT&T

I just traveled back from Los Angeles for the Apple “Pro and Tell” event, and the in-flight internet was so slow I just gave up on doing work. (Come on, Starlink!)

So instead I sat back, relaxed and caught up on ‘The Diplomat.’ It was awesome having a 7.6-inch screen at my disposal to watch the intrigue unfold. And I got really sucked into the action during a particularly perilous episode, with rich colors and lots of detail.

Another plus is the YouTube TV app. I love being able to watch four channels at once in a grid view, just as you can with Android foldables.

Sign up to the Tom's iGuide weekly newsletter with coverage on everything from product launches to software updates, this is your go-to source for the latest updates on all the best Apple content.

Yes, it’s long overdue, but I really appreciate being able to run apps side by side. For example, I get emails all the time about upcoming meetings and appointments, and I like being able to pull up Gmail in one window next to Google Calendar in another. It just makes my day easier.

I also upload images all the time to our dedicated photo room in Slack, and it’s great that I can just drag and drop images from the Photos app into this chat. Plus, you can just tap the middle of this split view to save the app pair.

If you’re addicted to doom scrolling, you might not want to get the iPhone Duo… It’s that addictive. Videos look pretty good on the cover screen, but on the big screen they’re way more immersive in portrait mode. And it’s especially cool that you can see the comments on the right when in landscape mode and they stay up as you keep scrolling.

I’ve been generally impressed with the iPhone Duo’s cameras, despite the lack of a dedicated telephoto lens. For example, the Duo took a gorgeous shot of the Los Angeles skyline just after sunset with deep blue, orange, yellow and red all coming through.

The iPhone Duo also did a great job of taking this shot of pumpkins in a large cornucopia, bringing out a surprising amount of detail in the shadows.

One of the benefits of the iPhone Duo is that it’s compact enough when closed that you can slip it into your front pocket. And it fits just fine. But I noticed while walking around that it weighed down that pocket.

The actual weight difference isn’t huge at 8.96 ounces (254 grams) for the iPhone Duo versus 8.22 ounces (233 grams) for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, but it’s enough to be noticeable and a bit annoying. I had to tighten my belt an extra notch so my pants wouldn’t fall down, and in many cases I wound up putting the Duo in my back pocket instead.

I give Apple some credit for making Split View multitasking on the iPhone Duo so intuitive. You just swipe up on an app and park it on the left or right side, then add another app.

However, the moment you flip from landscape to portrait view the app pair goes away. This is not the case on Samsung’s Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra. The only multitasking you can do in portrait mode is putting a video window on top of another open app.

I really loved reviewing and showing off photos I took on the iPhone Duo on its big display, but taking photos feels awkward. And it’s not just because the display is so large. I actually would like a large viewfinder at times.

The problem is that the Duo takes portrait photos in landscape mode and landscape mode pics in portrait mode, which is counterintuitive. You get used to it but it’s disorientating at first.

If I was designing the iPhone Duo 2, the first thing I would do is move the volume buttons. They’re on the top of the phone, which I find awkward to use. It’s not too bad with the phone closed but it’s of a stretch with the main display open. Personally, I would rather lose the Camera Control button or put that up top instead.

While many developers have been updating their apps for the iPhone Duo at a fairly fast clip, I’m bewildered that so many apps are not optimized at all.

For example, Google Calendar is a downright disaster on the iPhone Duo. There are huge black bars on the left and right side. The same thing goes for Google Drive. Google has optimized other apps. For example, YouTube and YouTube TV show the whole screen.

But even Gmail is half-assed on the Duo. It fills the display but you don’t get a two-column layout like you do on the Galaxy Z Fold 8. LinkedIn is another example. You would think they would have updated their app by now.

I can see why Apple chose to move the dock to the right side and menus and controls for apps. With such a wide front display, it would be tricky to reach across to the bottom left, for example. But that doesn’t mean this UI change is a success.

When you have just 5.4 inches to play with, taking up that much room in every app seems like a waste. Check out Instagram, for example, which has been fully optimized on the iPhone Duo. The right-hand strip means there’s less room for watching videos compared to the Fold 8.

The situation is even worse with apps that have a black bar on the right side, such as TikTok. And then you have apps whose right-hand menu covers the content as you scroll. Maybe Apple should just move all the controls to the bottom and allow developers to hide them, revealing them with a swipe or tap?

After giving up my iPhone 17 Pro Max for the iPhone Duo for two weeks, I feel like Apple has delivered a foldable phone that is (mostly) well designed. I really like having a huge display on the go that folds up into a more compact design. It’s like having an iPad Mini in your pocket, even if it weighs me down a little.

I also like the quality cameras, split-view multitasking, and consuming vertical video. However, I’m pretty shocked that very high profile developers have not fully updated their apps yet, which can make the Duo feel unfinished. And I don’t agree with some of Apple’s own design and UI decisions.

Do I think you should wait for an iPhone Duo 2? Not necessarily. I think the iPhone Duo is compelling, but I might wait for Apple and its partners to work out some of the early kinks before forking over two grand.

As a fitness expert in my 40s, my priorities have definitely changed. Yes, I still want to build muscle and feel strong, but I'm increasingly interested in exercises that challenge my balance, test my coordination and help me stay agile for the long haul.

I want to move well, in as many different directions as possible, for as long as possible. Because for me, it's no longer just about lifting heavy weights. It's about building a body that can move well and cope with life. And it turns out celebrity trainer Simone De La Rue thinks along similar lines.

The former professional dancer and founder of Body By Simone has worked with an impressive list of A-listers, including Taylor Swift, Jennifer Garner and Gigi Hadid, and recently shared a full-body compound exercise designed to challenge strength, balance and coordination in one go.

There’s quite a lot going on, but that’s exactly why I like it.

You’re strengthening your glutes, quads and hamstrings as you lunge, working your shoulders and arms as you press the weights overhead, then challenging the stabilizing muscles around your hips as you move laterally.

Your core has to work throughout to keep you stable and controlled, while the little hop to the side adds another challenge, asking the muscles around your hips, knees and ankles to power you up, then help you land safely again.

It also gets your balance and coordination involved: two things that become increasingly important as you get older.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Want to give it a go? Grab a pair of dumbbells and follow the steps below.

A post shared by Lucy Miller (@lucycmiller_)

The trick here is to break the move down and practice each part separately. There are several movements to coordinate, so start with lighter weights until you can move smoothly from the split squat into the press and lateral hop without losing your balance or letting your knees collapse inward.

Aim for two sets of six to eight repetitions on each side, using light dumbbells until you've mastered the move.

There’s a lot packed into one move. Here’s why I’ve added it to my strength workouts:

This is the big one. Rather than isolating a single muscle group, you’re asking several to work together.

The split squat targets your glutes, quads and hamstrings, while the overhead press works your shoulders and arms. Your core has to stabilize your torso as you move between the two.

For me, that makes it a great option when I want to get more from one exercise rather than spending hours in the gym.

Split squats already reduce your base of support compared with a regular squat. Add an overhead press and lateral movement, and your body has a lot more to deal with.

You need to stay stable as your weight shifts and your arms move overhead, which makes this as much a balance and coordination challenge as a strength exercise.

It’s a known fact that balance can decline as we get older, so exercises that challenge balance alongside strength are becoming a regular and important part of my own workouts.

It works your body in more than one direction

Most of us spend plenty of time moving forward and backward, whether that’s walking, running, or doing exercises such as squats and lunges.

Moving sideways recruits the muscles responsible for stabilizing your hips, including your gluteus medius. Strong hip stabilizers are important for controlling the pelvis and keeping the lower body stable when you walk, run, or stand on one leg.

You’ll find that the hop to the side takes a little effort to start with; your foot almost doesn’t want to jump out to the side, but it doesn’t take long to click, and you just really have to think about it, which I like when training. It's challenging. Think deep mind-muscle connection.

It makes your core work harder than you might think

You know those standing abs moves that we often talk about? Well, this is a great example. Your core is active throughout because it has to work to keep your torso stable during the split squat, stop you wobbling as you change direction and hop and provide a solid base as you press the dumbbells overhead. There’s a lot going on here.

You’ll probably notice it even more as you fatigue, which is why I started with a lighter pair of dumbbells and kept the entire movement controlled rather than overloading my body and losing form.

There’s no shortage of exercises to keep you strong as you get older, but I like this one because it combines so many things I want from my training in one sequence: strength, balance, coordination and mobility.

It’s also surprisingly challenging. You don't need particularly heavy dumbbells to feel your shoulders and legs working, and adding the overhead press and lateral step means your core rarely gets a chance to switch off.

Would I replace my squats and deadlifts with it? No. Those big compound lifts allow me to go heavier, which is crucial for building and maintaining strength as I get older. But as an accessory exercise in a full-body strength session, this is definitely one I’ll be keeping in my repertoire.

#3402. Shrinking season 4 just got exciting release timing update

Shrinking just aired season 3 earlier this year, but all signs point to a refreshingly quick return, as one of the show’s stars just confirmed season 4 is officially done filming.

TV’s streaming era has brought a lot of advantages over linear TV, but undoubtedly one drawback is that shows tend to have much longer waits between seasons.

Traditional broadcast television usually schedules shows to premiere in the fall and run through the spring, then return after a short summer break for a new season in the fall.

In streaming, viewers are shocked when a show comes back after only a year.

Apple TV has slowly been getting better at this. Slow Horses is the best example, but another recent one is Your Friends & Neighbors. And we’re seeing signs of other series getting quicker turnarounds between seasons, including Shrinking.

Shrinking aired its season 3 finale this April, and by May we heard that filming on season 4 was about to start.

Now Jessica Williams, the star who plays Gaby, has confirmed that season 4 has officially wrapped production. This means the series will almost certainly return in early 2027.

On a show like Shrinking, post-production is a much quicker process than with series that are heavy on CGI and other special effects. So we could see Shrinking season 4 premiere in late January, exactly one year after season 3 debuted.

More conservatively, the show returning by spring 2027 seems a safe bet.

Nothing, the upstart U.K. brand that makes products like phones, smartwatches, and headphones, has quickly become one of my favorite players in tech. As you know ... Lindsay allegedly strangled her three children -- 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan -- in January 2023 before jumping from a second-story window, leaving her paralyzed from the waist down.

Her first murder trial ended in a mistrial in September ... and she's due back in court Monday to learn whether prosecutors will try her again.

Meanwhile, Lindsay is suing 11 medical professionals, claiming they failed to properly treat her psychiatric condition before the killings. Her attorneys insist she was suffering from postpartum psychosis ... allegations the defendants dispute.

Lindsay remains in a Massachusetts psychiatric facility and has pleaded not guilty to the murder charges.

With the ongoing “RAMageddon”, the rapid development of data centers and the pure vitriol brought against “AI slop” these days, I can see why AI skeptics are hoping for an AI industry market crash.

Once the news of China’s AI sector suffering a massive market crash that wiped out $480 billion reached my timeline, I started thinking about the possibility of that event coming to fruition in the US. There’s been so much speculation over the very existence of an AI bubble, when it could finally burst and what could happen to the several US sector & the tech itself if a crash took place.

Since I’m so prone to asking the likes of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity hot-button questions, I knew it was time for me to see what they thought about those three topics. So I brought this loaded set of questions to their attention: “Is there really an AI bubble? If so, when is it going to burst and what will happen if it does?

Here are some of the most intriguing responses each chatbot gave me, with one of them even drawing comparisons between a possible AI market crash and the infamous dot-com crash from 2000 to 2002.

OpenAI’s chatbot was first up at bat for my latest inquisitive session about AI. It made sure to point out that there are clear signs that there is an AI bubble and that parts of it may be on the verge of popping. But it also noted that an AI crash isn’t such a sure bet:

Yes, there are credible reasons to worry that parts of the AI industry are in a bubble — but that doesn't mean AI itself is a fad, or that a crash is inevitable. The most useful way to think about it is to separate two questions:

- Is AI valuable? AI tools can already help people write, code, analyze information, automate tasks and create content.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

- Are investors paying too much for AI? Potentially. Companies can be building genuinely useful technology while investors simultaneously overestimate how quickly it will generate profits.

That distinction is important because the dot-com boom of the late 1990s offers a useful comparison: the internet transformed the economy, but many internet companies still failed when their valuations outran their businesses. The AI industry could experience something similar — a correction in investment and valuations even as the technology continues to improve.

As for when the AI bubble could burst, ChatGPT stated that no one can reliably predict its occurrence. The main scenario it alluded to as the worst one was set from 2027 through 2029, as it explained how a serious reckoning could come to pass if its revenue for the AI industry fails to keep up with the infrastructure spending from private sectors going into it. Or if customers discover that AI delivered less measurable value than they originally expected.

To wrap up its investigation into the matter, ChatGPT stated that the central question at the heart of the AI bubble-bursting topic is whether the money it generates can eventually justify the money that’s being spent on it. If yes, then it noted that this current AI investment boom will be looked back on as an expensive yet productive period of technological development. If no, then AI investors, startups, lenders and workers could be dealt a very bad hand while the technology itself continues to advance in some way.

As I went through Gemini’s detailed breakdowns of its explanations to my questions, its comparisons to the dot-com crash and the AI bubble possibly bursting caught my attention the most. It pointed to three ways in which both events share striking similarities:

Gemini also made sure to point out a key difference between the fallout of the dot-com crash and the possible AI bubble finally bursting. It acknowledged that several dot-com firms ceased to exist after the dot-com crash, while the AI bubble bursting wouldn’t be too catastrophic for some of the tech leaders backing the tech, since they have other worthy investments (Amazon with e-commerce and Microsoft with software as a service, for example).

While those companies would face some financial struggles from the AI bubble bursting, Gemini noted that a complete shutdown of their businesses due to it happening wouldn’t likely occur.

Anthropic’s chatbot dived into the possibilities of an AI bubble existing by detailing why everyone’s so worried about it bursting, why an AI bubble may not fully exist at the moment and a possible timeline for when it could burst:

Perplexity’s response to my questions stated that there are notable signs of an AI bubble bursting, but those same signs don’t fully paint the picture of the AI industry being close to a crash:

There are credible signs of an AI investment bubble, especially in parts of startup funding and infrastructure spending—but that does not establish that the entire industry is overvalued or that a crash is imminent. Nobody can reliably tell you when it will burst, or whether it will end in a sudden crash rather than a long, uneven adjustment. The biggest distinction is between a stock-market bust and a debt crisis: both could hurt, but the latter would spread much further through the economy.

To back up its reasoning, Perplexity brought up a report from The Olympian that offers debates about the existence of an AI bubble. It also mentioned a report from a prominent management consulting firm to provide an assessment of when the possible AI bubble could burst:

With shocking news hitting my timeline about AI investments going bad, it’s easy to envision a world where the AI bubble finally bursting comes to pass.

With Google’s recent massive loss of $500 billion due to its AI search feature disrupting ad sales, the odds of that aforementioned event taking place are getting higher and higher. All four chatbots do agree that there are sectors of the AI industry that are in danger of collapsing, while Gemini highlighted the clear comparisons between the AI bubble bursting and the 2000s dot-com crash.

After comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity, I walked away from my latest chatbot questionnaire session knowing that the AI industry shows signs of plunging badly. But as for when that moment could take place, no one truly knows.

iOS 27 brought a variety of big improvements to Shared Albums. And now iOS 27.2 has introduced four more.

One complication introduced by AI is that it can be hard to know if an image is real or AI-generated.

This challenge extends to AI-edited photos too, which might have key details changed by tools like iOS 27’s Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up features in Photos.

Apple is tackling the issue with its new Reference Image feature in iPhone 18 Pro, and also through a software enhancement that rolled out in iOS 27.2.

Per Apple, its latest software update adds the following:

Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground

SynthID is a cross-platform standard developed by Google that embeds unnoticeable digital watermarks into AI-modified photos. Users won’t see a visible watermark, but anyone who checks for a SynthID marker will find it.

#3393. BigXthaPlug Wrestles With Success on ‘Better Over Time’

BigXthaPlug, a Dallas, Texas, vocalist with a deep, grainy, and authoritative mic presence, is one of the most intriguing voices in years. He’s the rare twentysomething mainstream rapper that actually raps. He doesn’t rely on an android-like croon like Don Toliver or hearty “trap-soul” laments like Rod Wave. Instead, he spits hard and from the chest, his momentum hitting the ears like NFL linebacker Myles Garrett shoving wide receivers into gridiron grass. And happily, at least for old heads disenchanted with the state of modern rap, he frequently pays homage to OGs past and present. On 6WA, a consistently entertaining project with his 600 Entertainment crew released last March, he invited Texas-émigré-turned-West-Coast-pioneer the D.O.C. to offer a benediction, then referenced the old-school hardness of Too $hort and the late Eazy-E. On his new album, Better Over Time, producers Tony Coles and Charley Cooks sample the Notorious B.I.G.’s “Sky’s the Limit” while Leon Thomas revives 112’s classic chorus: “Sky is the limit and you know that you can have what you want, be what you want.”

Ironically, given his meteoric rise, Better Over Time often presents fame and fortune as a mirage that can’t mask lifelong pain. In an RS cover story on BigXthaPlug earlier this year, journalist Eric Diep wrote, “He’s in better spirits now, and not making sad music anymore.” Perhaps Better Over Time isn’t as persistently melancholy as I Hope You’re Happy, his Billboard Top 10-charting suite of broken-hearted collaborations with Nashville’s top country stars that helped land him a spot at the 2025 CMA Awards, where he performed “Pray Hard” with Luke Combs. Yet his frustration with seeing his friends and neighbors turn him into an object of gossip and envy after he successfully overcame poverty simmers until it nearly overwhelms what should be a glorious, Life After Death-styled victory lap. Much like on Baby Keem’s Ca$ino, another recent rap epic undone by its author’s inability to overcome lingering trauma, BigX can’t always navigate around his unnamed haters. His main instinct is to pull out a wad of bills and fling it in their faces. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Despite the peevish tone of Better Over Time, BigX remains a ferociously magnetic presence, someone who retains a listener’s focus with ease, whether it’s alone or with collaborators like GloRilla, who snaps with canny sharpness alongside him on “FAF.” Rap aesthetes have blanched at some of BigX’s arena-pop moves, like pairing with Ava Max on Better Over Time’s advance single, the airy and declamatory “Burn.” But “Burn” also underlines his expansive nature and his ability to encompass different sonic moods without cynicism. (The single even gives BigX an opportunity to celebrate his cover glow-up, as he raps, “Who from my state front-page Rolling Stone and proudly rep they city?”) Elsewhere, he blithely offers a chipmunk-soul delight reminiscent of early Kanye West on “Lite” while comparing himself to Jodeci and “Lil Wayne on Tha Carter III” and dominates a cipher with critical favorites Babyface Ray and Lil Yachty on “Believe.” Dark clouds may be slowly distorting BigX’s frame of mind, but moments of pleasure often shine through. “Been collectin’ this green/This big n—- like salad with dressin’,” he delightfully brags on “Cracced.”

BigX frequently alludes to the importance of family. The first voice on Better Over Time belongs to his mother. “It seems like just yesterday, you was fighting and getting kicked out of school and shit. Now look at your ass,” she says on “Stand on Business.” “You’re a boss, a legend.” He talks about making money to feed his two children and support his extended family and boasts on “Da Fucc” that he’s spent so much money on guns that “my grandma strapped with a stick.” “Million-dollar n—-, shit I got, you can’t afford this/Tryna stay off the Forbes list ‘cause that’s when they gon’ want shit,” he says on “Peace of Mind.” However, a few cuts later, he contradicts himself on “Give It All” when he raps, “I want the billions, the trillions, and whatever else, ‘cause the millions, I already got.” Big numbers like that will certainly put him on the IRS’s radar. It’s also proof that BigX is working out his ideas and beliefs in real time. Better Over Time should give him an opportunity to expunge his anguish and, if not necessarily heal, then find clarity on why his preternatural talent has brought a mixture of blessings and frustration. He’s had plenty of success, from Drake and Beyoncé cosigns to Wingstop licensing his 2024 hit “The Largest” for a widely aired 2025 commercial starring NBA sharpshooter Jalen Green. So why does he feel overwhelmed like “a slave with all these chains”?  Trending Stories Michael Douglas Gives Update on Jack Nicholson: He's 'Well' But Has 'Disappeared' Martha Stewart 'Distressed' by Backlash to Her Homeless Halloween Costume My Chemical Romance Tops the Billboard 200 With 20-Year-Old Album Harry Styles Ended His Historic Madison Square Garden Run — And This Song Captured It All

As he grinds away over the album’s 42 minutes, lucidity seems distant. “Wonder if I said fuck it and stayed in the streets sellin’ dope,” he fumes on “Lately F Rap.” “Would them n—-s still speak on my name for some clout?/Probably not, ‘cause I wouldn’t have an image.” On “Heal Me,” a cut that almost drowns in Florida singer Fridayy’s blandly Christian fervor, BigX admits that he’s riding in a “double R” Rolls-Royce:  “My rug’s been damp from all these tears/But I been fightin’ how I feel for some years/I think it’s time I take this moment to heal.” Still, the final track centers on an interpolation of Harry Nilsson’s “One.” As producer Bandplay sings, “One is the loneliest number that there ever was,” BigX raps, “I’m out by myself all alone/Don’t feel welcomed in what I call home.” It’s a bit of a downer.

It’s easy to dismiss BigX’s anguish as the familiar pop trope of a rich man’s blues or, as Biggie once put it, mo’ money, mo’ problems. But he’s only 28 and clearly struggling under the glare of increased expectations from fans, his community, and the music industry. He may still be prone to youthful mistakes, as an August DWI arrest on unlawful firearm and marijuana possession charges suggested. Better Over Time implicitly promises that he’ll keep evolving in the years to come, even as it withholds the satisfaction of hearing him find closure now.

Unfortunately, rats don't hibernate in the cold

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you’ve ever had a rat problem, then you'll know there are many ways you can prevent these pesky creatures from entering your home — especially in the fall and winter.

Yes, the National Pest Management Association (NPMA) recently released a statistic showing that 45% of all annual rodent infestations happen during the fall and winter months.

So if you haven't thought about it before, here's what to do in October to keep rats from coming to life in November or December.

Not only is the thought of a rat living in your house spine-crawling, but we all know that they can carry diseases. And they eat anything in sight — wires, wood, and food.

They also don't need an open invitation to come inside; a large hole or an open window is enough to encourage them in. They're the opposite of escape artists; let's call them entrance assassins.

The two main culprits in the U.S. are Norway rats and Roof rats, and in cold weather, their survival depends on where they live and feed. So when the temperature drops, rats head closer to the heat — if not indoors, they may go toward the insulation beneath your subfloor, up into your roof (because heat rises), or into a cozy garage.

Did you know?Rats can squeeze through a gap that’s the size of a quarter; for mice, it’s the size of a dime.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Lawns and hedgingLet's start outside because yes, it all makes a huge difference. This might be music to your ears, or you may roll your eyes, but a trimmed lawn is an easy, quick way to deter rats.

The same goes for any foliage: if you cut it back, it won't attract rats, but the problem starts when it becomes overgrown. While English Ivy looks amazing, in winter it becomes the perfect climbing ladder for these creatures, especially if it’s attached to your house wall. Therefore, check the gap between your hedging and any greenery near an open window.

Open trashAs for your trash cans, cracked or warped containers may attract rats, which can quickly become a huge problem. It's time to replace them with new ones. Worse still, is if you keep your trash bags outside instead of in a can.

Feeding the birds, and the ratsLove to feed the birds? You might soon change your mind. Bird feeders attract rats this season, which is a shame for the birds, but realistically, you may need to wait until spring. Otherwise, you can feed them huskless seed and use a squirrel guard instead.

A game-changer for safe bird feeding in the winter, this also means that those pesky squirrels can't take any of their food. Easy to install and currently on sale, get it now or regret it later.

Rats don't hibernate. They try to survive winter in any way they can. As with the hot spots I've already mentioned, when it comes to indoor living, rats tend to hide in warm spots.

Behind your giant refrigerator, a dishwasher, or dryer is a safe place for a rat to seek warmth. They love furnaces and hot water pipes, too. Anything that oozes warmth in an otherwise cold room. And don’t forget your loft — any fiberglass up there provides a lovely warm bed for them.

However, rats might also head straight to your garage, especially if you store extra food or pet food there, so it's worth rethinking what you store and where. If you can't change the storage spot, keep food in airtight, rat-proof metal containers. Inside your home, store food in plastic packets, away from your garage, and ideally move it to an airtight plastic or glass container.

For any external doors, like the one from your home into your garage, it's smart to invest in a few rodent-proof door sweeps. Just in case they make their way inside through a tiny door crack. They will also be handy when you turn on the heating, since they’ll keep valuable heat from escaping.

Heavy rain also drives rats indoors, so keep ahead of the weather forecast and secure your home before rats become a problem.

Amazon's Choice for a reason, you can buy a 4-pack to save more money and use these in more places than one. Easy to screw into your door, there's a rubber strip along the bottom of the stopper that ensures it is fully rat-proof. It can even seal gaps 1-inch wide.

If you religiously search your home for holes and fill them, ready for rat season, then bear in mind that what you fill them with matters. Rats can chew through plastic, rubber, or standard vinyl caulk. Instead, copper mesh wool is totally rat-proof. You can then seal it with silicone caulk, so it looks better.

You can only buy this in a large roll, but truly, you never know when you'll need it. Included is literally everything you need to secure your home from rodents, including safety gloves, scissors, and a packing tool to help push it into a hole or two.

It's about the size of a carry-on suitcase and weighs close to 50 pounds, so it's not something you'd strap to your back, but it fits easily in a car trunk. The battery itself is built to last, rated for 4,000 charges before it starts losing any noticeable capacity. Performance-wise, DJI says the 2,048Wh capacity can keep a refrigerator running for up to 40 hours during a home power outage, charge a laptop 18 times, or power a projector for 18 hours. Those numbers line up with what you’d expect from a unit this size, and they make it useful for both emergencies and planned outdoor use.

You also get a solid mix of ports—there are three AC outlets, a 30-amp port for heavier appliances or RV setups, multiple USB-C ports (including a 140W option for laptops), and DJI’s own SDC ports for direct drone charging. If you use DJI gear, that alone makes life easier in the field, notes this Mashable review. Recharging is also fast for a battery this size. Plugged into a wall outlet, it can go from empty to full in about 90 minutes. You can also top it up with solar panels or from your car, which makes it workable for longer trips. Rounding out its features is its companion app, which lets you check its battery level from your phone without having to walk over to it, a small thing that turns out to be pretty convenient. Note that this unit has no built-in light, which is something many competing power stations include.

Everything awaits below, alongside some charging gear deals like the Belkin Qi2.2 25W UltraCharge 2-in-1 Foldable Charging Station down at $50.

We have had an extended run of deals on Apple’s best earbuds lately, and after jumping back up closer to full price yesterday, Amazon has decided to keep the ball rolling with a solid20% discount on AirPods Pro 3.

Amazon is now offering Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 down at $199.99 shipped. That’s actually $1 more than they were through last week, but we are still talking about a solid 20% discount here at nearly $50 off the list price.

Alongside the current AirPods Pro 3 at $50 off, one of today’s featured deals at Woot delivers AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation down at $99 shipped. That’s a sizable 45% price drop on the previous-generation buds and easily one of the best prices ever, but you can score the new AirPods 5 with ANC from $129.

AirPods 4 with ANC carried a $179 list price before being replaced by the AirPods 5 lineup this past September. Today’s deal is 45% off the original list price and one of the best deals we have tracked on the buds to date – the Woot listing is in brand new condition, but it ships with a 90-day Woot warranty.

This is matching last year’s particularly popular and extremely notable Amazon Black Friday price, but the new AirPods 5 are available now and you can score the entry-level set that also happens to include ANC this time around for just $29 more.
